title: Guardian Of The Night
author: William Saville
content:
The streetlights flickered against the encroaching darkness, their pale glow struggling to illuminate the cracked pavement. Ava stood at the edge of the park, her heart racing not from fear but from exhilaration. Just a few weeks ago, the thought of walking home after sunset sent chills down her spine, a reminder of all the dangers lurking in the shadows. But tonight, those shadows felt different; familiar, welcoming even.

She remembered her life before the change: the suffocating fear that clung to her like a heavy shroud, the memories of late-night encounters that left her feeling vulnerable and small. It had been a Friday evening, the air thick with laughter and the clinking of glasses. Ava had never imagined her life would change so drastically, nor that she would be forced to walk the thin line between life and death. That night, she'd been out with friends, strolling through the city, laughter carrying into the still night air. After leaving her friends, she felt the familiar prickling sensation of being watched as she walked home alone.

Then, the sound of footsteps echoed behind her. At first, she dismissed it, thinking it was just her imagination, but the feeling grew, heavy and unsettling. Instinct prickled along her spine as she looked over her shoulder, heart quickening. Ava felt her skin crawl, as if warning her that something was dangerously close.

As she turned the corner, a figure emerged from the dark, moving with a silence that made her blood run cold, a predatory grin stretching across his face. He grabbed her, dragging her into a dimly lit alleyway before she could scream. The air was stale, the smell of garbage and neglect suffocating. She struggled against him, but he was stronger, his grip like iron.

“Please, let me go!” Ava gasped, panic surging through her veins as he pressed her against the cold brick wall.

“Not a chance,” he sneered, his breath hot against her face. “You’re going to be my little snack.”

In a dizzying blur, he pressed his mouth to her neck. The sharp pain of his teeth pierced her skin, and she felt the warmth of her blood flowing, pooling around her consciousness as darkness began to seep in. Each heartbeat weakened until it slowed to a thudding echo. As the world faded, fear gave way to an unsettling numbness, and her vision blurred.

Just as she thought it was over, he pulled back, laughing maniacally. “You look so pale! But don’t worry; I have just the thing to make you feel better,” he taunted. With a swift motion, he cut into his own wrist and pressed it against her lips. “Drink, little bird. It’s either this or you die here.”

Ava’s instincts kicked in, the primal urge for survival overriding her horror. She drank deeply, the metallic taste of his blood mingling with the remnants of her own. It burned as it slid down her throat, igniting a fire within her that twisted and roared. A surge of strength coursed through her, but it came with agony; every nerve ending screamed as the transformation began. Her body contorted in ways she couldn’t comprehend, writhing in pain as darkness enveloped her, her screams swallowed by the night.

Left alone in the alley, she clutched her stomach, gasping for air as the world faded to black. It felt like she was being torn apart, the last threads of her humanity fraying under the strain of her new existence.

When she awoke, the moon hung high in the sky, casting a silver glow that illuminated her surroundings. The alley felt foreign yet familiar, a place she no longer recognized. As she pulled herself to her feet, she caught sight of her reflection in a shattered piece of glass. Her eyes glowed crimson, her skin pale and smooth, the remnants of the girl she once was slipping away like sand through her fingers.

She felt stronger, faster; yet hollowed, a part of her life stolen by the bite. She was no longer the same Ava who had laughed with friends. She had become… something else.

The hunger hit her next, clawing and relentless. She could feel the thirst pulsing in her veins, urging her to seek out blood, to feast. She gritted her teeth, fists clenching as she fought the dark craving that threatened to consume her. No, she told herself. She refused to be a monster.

A purpose surged within her, one she couldn’t explain but knew she couldn’t ignore. She wasn’t just a survivor; she was something more. She had been chosen, in a cruel twist of fate, to protect the lives she had once belonged to. She would walk among humans, guarding them from the predators lurking in the night.

Ava soon discovered her senses were heightened; every sound and movement amplified. With newfound agility, she moved through the city like a phantom, gliding silently over rooftops and through shadows. It was exhilarating. But as she roamed the streets, she witnessed the vulnerabilities of women walking alone at night; the same fear she had felt just hours before.

As she continued her journey that night, her throat burned with thirst. She hunted until she saw a man lurking outside a bar, waiting, eyes scanning the crowd; a predator in search of prey. Anger bubbled within her, a visceral reaction to the darkness she had once endured. Ava watched as he approached a woman leaving the bar, her laughter abruptly cut off as he grabbed her arm.

In a flash, Ava was upon him, her movements swift and calculated. “Hey!” she shouted, her voice ringing out with authority she had never felt before. The man turned, surprise etched across his features. “Let her go!”

The confrontation was swift and brutal. With every ounce of strength coursing through her veins, she tackled him to the ground, pinning him beneath her. “You’re not going to hurt anyone tonight,” she hissed, her fangs bared as the thrill of her new identity coursed through her.

After ensuring he wouldn’t threaten another woman, Ava stood over him, the adrenaline coursing through her like wildfire. She felt powerful; no longer a victim, but a guardian of the night. She pinned him to the ground with her high heel, piercing his throat, swooped down, and drank her fill as his would-be victim thanked her dark angel, and fled.

As the initial shock of her transformation began to fade, Ava found herself grappling with her newfound abilities and the overwhelming thirst that gnawed at her relentlessly. The once-familiar world now seemed alien, every sound and scent amplified to an almost unbearable degree. She spent countless nights testing her limits, pushing the boundaries of her new existence.

At first, Ava's heightened senses were disorienting. The rustle of leaves sounded like a roar, the faintest light pierced her eyes, and every scent; especially blood; was intoxicating. One evening, perched on a rooftop, she discovered she could leap great distances, soaring from building to building with ease. The thrill of it was exhilarating, but the constant thirst was a reminder of the monster she could become.

In an abandoned warehouse, she tested her strength, lifting rusted machinery and crushing metal pipes with her bare hands. Her body was a paradox of fragility and power, each movement a dance between her old self and the creature she was becoming. She practiced blending into the shadows, moving with such silence that even the nocturnal animals were unaware of her presence. Yet, every small victory was accompanied by the relentless hunger, a burning need that only one thing could quench.

As she roamed the city, Ava began to notice patterns; places where predators lurked, preying on the vulnerable. Her first real test came when she saw a man dragging a young woman into a deserted alley. The woman's muffled cries echoed in Ava's ears, sparking a rage that burned away her hesitation. She moved swiftly, her newfound agility allowing her to close the distance in seconds.

The man barely had time to react before Ava's hands were around his throat, lifting him off the ground with ease. "Leave her alone," she growled, her voice carrying a menacing undertone. The man struggled, gasping for air, but Ava's grip was unrelenting. She could feel the terror emanating from him, his heartbeat pounding in her ears. It was intoxicating, but she focused on the woman, her priority. With a final warning glance, she released him, letting him stumble away, gasping for breath.

The woman looked up at Ava, a mixture of fear and gratitude in her eyes. "Thank you," she whispered, her voice trembling.

Ava nodded, her fangs still retracted. "Get home safe," she said softly, watching as the woman hurried away. The hunger gnawed at her, but she resisted until the girl was away, knowing she needed control over her instincts. As soon as her footsteps could be heard no more, she fed.

As the days turned into weeks, Ava refined her abilities and her resolve. She began hunting those who preyed on the weak, ensuring they would never harm anyone again. One night, she encountered a gang harassing a young man in a dark alley. Without hesitation, she intervened, her movements precise and deadly. Each predator she took down fed her thirst, but it also fueled her purpose.

But she had never felt more powerful than she had last night. The vampire who had attacked her was there again, watching from the shadows of an alleyway cluttered with abandoned furniture near a grimy dumpster. She had been perched above, scanning the streets from the rooftops in search of her next meal when she saw him. His cold eyes roamed the streets, already marking his next victim. Seeing him again; the one who had stolen her humanity; ignited a blaze of rage within her.

“He will not harm another soul,” she whispered, the words burning with conviction. She leapt from her high vantage point, landing smoothly on the sidewalk beside him.

She approached him, each step fueled by her desire for justice. “Looking for someone?” she challenged, her voice steady, edged with a simmering anger.

He turned, a smirk curling on his face. “Ah, my creation,” he murmured, arrogance dripping from each word. “Come to join me?”

Ava’s resolve hardened like steel. “No. I’m here to stop you.”

He laughed, low and mocking, but she stood her ground. She was quick this time, prepared. They clashed in the night, their movements swift, fierce, and unrelenting. Each strike she landed echoed with defiance, a newfound strength pulsing through her.

In the heat of the fight, she spotted a wooden chair discarded by the dumpster. She seized it, snapping off a sturdy leg with ease, and drove it into his chest. His eyes widened, shock frozen on his face as his body began to crack and crumble. Finally, he disintegrated into dust, leaving only silence and a strange, calm satisfaction in her wake.

As the night resumed its silence, Ava stood alone, the streets empty save for the faint echo of her former life. She had been thrust into a new existence, forced to abandon the simplicity she once knew. But now, she had a purpose.

Turning toward the shadows, Ava vowed to guard the world she had once known, to be the protector she had needed on that fateful night. And though the thirst remained, always lurking, she knew she would resist. She had become a creature of the night, but she would be a guardian, not a monster.

Now, standing at the park's edge, she pulled her long, dark hair into a loose ponytail, tucking a few rebellious strands behind her ear. The leather jacket she wore felt like a second skin, imbued with the confidence she had longed for. She scanned the streets, her senses sharper than ever, every rustle of leaves and distant laughter vibrating through her.

Tonight, she had a mission. Her friends; Sarah, Mia, and Jess; were waiting at their usual spot, the old bar at the corner of Maple and 3rd. With a determined smile, Ava stepped into the night, her heels clicking rhythmically on the pavement. Each step felt like a declaration of her new purpose: she was no longer a target; she was a protector.

She had known her friends her entire life. Growing up together in New York, they had gone to the same schools and shared countless memories. Despite their different styles and interests, nothing ever broke their bond of sisterhood. They were the first ones Ava told about her transformation into a vampire, a revelation that took weeks of courage to share. She’d tested her new powers on herself, once she finally felt safe enough to tell them, she did so by stabbing her hand with a fork to show her rapid healing to her friends. Sarah had fainted, Mia had bombarded her with a million questions, and Jess had been surprisingly calm.

Ava was studying to be a doctor, with dreams of joining Doctors Without Borders and currently volunteering at Planned Parenthood. Mia was a graphic designer, Sarah a photographer, and Jess a veterinarian. All of them came from wealthy families who worked from nothing to have what they had, so they appreciated everything the world gave them, and they were raised with those same ideals as their parents. They did a lot of volunteer work together growing up, and still did a lot of homeless outreach. They were an eclectic mix, but their love for each other was unwavering. Even in their early twenties, they still lived together, often having sleepovers in the living room with blanket forts and pizza.

Inside the bar, the energy buzzed; a mix of laughter, clinking glasses, and the eclectic sounds of karaoke echoing through the air. Neon lights danced across the walls, casting vibrant hues over the Formica tables. Ava and her friends settled into a cozy booth, the faux leather seats slightly worn but comfortable, a sanctuary from the chaos outside.

“What’s our first song?” Sarah shouted over the noise, her excitement palpable as she scanned the karaoke songbook, her golden curls bouncing with each movement. She danced briefly with silly energy, taking off her pink crochet top to reveal a black tank underneath that matched her black mini skirt. Ava glanced at Mia, with her blue pixie cut hair and bright green lipstick, such a perfect contrast to her spiked black jacket, and Jess, sporting a vintage AC/DC band tee and ripped blue jeans that hinted at her rebellious spirit.

“I vote for ‘I Will Survive’!” Jess suggested, her eyes sparkling mischievously. The others erupted into laughter, knowing Jess had a penchant for belting out empowering anthems.

“Only if I can sing the Gloria Gaynor part!” Mia chimed in, her voice rising above the chatter. They quickly agreed, and as the opening notes filled the air, they sprang to their feet, laughter spilling over as they joined the enthusiastic crowd.

As they sang, their voices harmonizing and clashing in all the right ways, the smells of greasy fries and sweet milkshakes wafted around them, blending into comforting nostalgia. Ava felt the warmth of the bar enveloping her, a stark contrast to the cool night air outside. The waitress, a bubbly girl with an infectious smile and a red and black apron, brought over a pitcher of margaritas, the salted rims glistening under the lights.

“Cheers to us!” Ava proclaimed, raising her glass as the others followed suit. They shared silly stories between songs, recounting embarrassing moments from their childhood, the laughter growing louder with every sip. “Oh God Sarah, remember that time when we played spin the bottle with your brother when we were bored and you got him and he tried to kiss you?”

“Ava, I am not nearly drunk enough for that story!” Sarah said, laughing and gulping down more of her margarita. “Besides, at least I didn't accidentally hook up with my cousin at a FUNERAL!”

“Heyyyy” Mia whined, playfully punching Sarah. “She was cute, I had no idea we were cousins, because my great-aunt had decided to write off that side of the family, and she was a really good kisser! Among other things…” Mia trailed off eyebrows wiggling mischievously while everyone else groaned and sipped their drinks. Ava took a look again at Mia’s eyes, which she had known were pretty, back when she was human. A deep blue with green in the center. But with vampire eyes, Mia’s eyes were breathtakingly beautiful, a dozen different shades of blue fire dancing out of a brilliant green haze with an inky black center. Ava was bisexual, but she'd never been attracted to any of her friends before, that had definitely changed. But she'd never act on it, their sisterhood was too important to her.

As they finished their first round of drinks, a group of rowdy patrons nearby took the stage, belting out a shockingly off-key rendition of “Sweet Caroline.” The room erupted in cheers, some patrons joining in on the “ba ba ba” parts while others groaned in exaggerated agony. “This is a nightmare!” Ava laughed, shaking her head as she grabbed her margarita.

When it was their turn again, they tackled “Dancing Queen,” their voices intertwining in harmony as they moved in time with the music, feeling the rhythm pulse through them. The atmosphere was electric, and for the first time in a long while, Ava felt completely at ease, the weight of her past slipping away with each note.

Amid the laughter and singing, a loud crash suddenly disrupted the revelry. A waitress stumbled back, her tray of drinks flying through the air after a drunk patron grabbed her butt as she passed. The drinks splattered everywhere, and a murmur of discontent rippled through the crowd.

Ava’s heart raced, instinct kicking in as she jumped from the booth. “Hey! What the hell?” she shouted, her voice cutting through the noise. She marched over to the drunken man, who was now chuckling with his friends, completely oblivious to the chaos he’d caused.

“Do you think that’s funny?” she demanded, hands on her hips, her glare fierce. The man blinked, a hint of confusion flashing across his face as he realized what he’d done. “It’s not a joke! You just disrespected her!” she continued, her voice steady but filled with intensity.

“I was just playing around,” he slurred, an angry grin spreading across his face.

“That’s not ‘playing around,’” Ava shot back. In that moment, she realized that her transformation wasn't just about strength; it was about standing up for others, reclaiming not only her own power but also becoming a voice for those who couldn’t speak up. Her heart raced with a fierce determination as she took a step closer, narrowing the distance between her and the man who had crossed a line.

“Look, I don’t care how much you’ve had to drink. That’s not acceptable behavior, and it never will be,” Ava stated firmly, her voice unwavering. The laughter and chatter in the bar faded into a hushed silence as the patrons turned their attention to the scene unfolding before them. Internally, Ava’s undead heart galloped and faltered, she was not used to behaving this way, and she still felt that old fear sometimes, but she knew what she must do and be now.

The drunken man’s grin faltered, and for a moment, he seemed to grasp the gravity of his actions. But his friends, egging him on, urged him to brush it off. “Come on, man, it was just a joke!” one of them shouted, trying to diffuse the tension.

Ava's gaze flicked to the waitress, who was attempting to clean up the mess with trembling hands, her cheeks flushed with embarrassment. “What’s your name?” Ava asked the waitress gently, her tone shifting from confrontational to supportive.

“Lila,” she whispered, glancing up with a mix of gratitude and surprise.

“Lila, you’re not alone. None of us are,” Ava declared, raising her voice slightly to ensure everyone could hear. “We’re here to stand together, not let people like him make us feel small.” The crowd murmured in agreement, nodding and exchanging encouraging glances.

With renewed courage, Ava turned back to the man. “You think you can just treat people like they’re objects? It’s disgusting,” she said, her voice cutting through the air. “You need to learn what respect really means.” The man’s bravado started to fade, his friends now growing quiet as they realized this was no longer a joke. Ava could see the shift in his demeanor, the fear creeping in as he glanced around, noticing the disapproving stares from the other patrons, and how Ava’s fangs had glinted in the neon lights, her eyes glowing redder as her anger rose.

Just as she thought he might apologize or back down, he sneered, trying to regain his composure. “You don’t know me. You think you can just lecture me?” Yet, she could sense his slight fear, and realized it was a show for his friends.

“I don’t need to know you to see that you’re weak,” Ava replied, her confidence surging. “Real strength comes from lifting others up, not tearing them down. And you; ” she pointed a finger at him, “; are nothing but a coward.”

A silence enveloped the bar, tension thick in the air. Lila, the waitress, looked at Ava with wide eyes, and Ava felt a surge of hope as she saw support blooming among the other patrons. The energy shifted from fear to defiance, a collective stand against the disrespect that had become all too common. The drunk man shifted uncomfortably, caught between anger and embarrassment. But before he could retort, one of his friends stepped in, clearly tired of the situation. “Come on, man. Let’s get out of here,” he muttered, pulling him away from the scene.

Ava watched as they stumbled out, their laughter fading into the night. The bar’s atmosphere shifted back to one of camaraderie and laughter, but a different kind of energy now filled the room; empowerment.

Returning to her friends, she felt the weight of what she had done. “You were amazing!” Sarah exclaimed, pulling her into a hug. “I can’t believe you stood up to him like that!”

Mia chimed in, “Yeah, Ava! You really showed him what’s up.” Jess nodded vigorously, her eyes bright with admiration.

Ava smiled, her heart swelling with a sense of belonging. “I couldn’t just let that go,” she replied, feeling the warmth of her friends' support. “We need to look out for each other. We all deserve to feel safe.”

As the night wore on, Ava found herself reflecting on how far she had come. Once a victim, now a protector; her transformation was about more than just strength; it was about community, resilience, and reclaiming the night for those who had felt its chill.

With every song sung and every laugh shared, Ava felt the pieces of her old self merging with the new. The past might have shaped her, but it no longer defined her. She was a force to be reckoned with, a guardian of those who felt lost, and she embraced that role wholeheartedly.

As they finally left the bar, Ava took Lila to the side and handed her $100 privately, away from prying eyes, causing the girl to bawl gratefully. Ava hugged her tightly and told her to call her if she was ever harassed again, and then stepped out onto the streets, linking arms with her friends. The moon hung bright in the sky, illuminating the streets with a gentle glow. Ava walked confidently, her friends by her side, ready to face whatever the night might bring. The darkness no longer felt like a threat; it felt like home.
